title: How Identity and Opinion Shape Political Sycophancy in LLMs
abstract: arXiv:2608.29198v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: As Large Language Models (LLMs) increasingly encourage users to disclose personal profiles for tailored assistance, measuring their political alignment becomes increasingly important. However, many existing benchmarks for assessing political behavior rely on closed-ended questions and do not fully capture how a model's stance may adapt to user-provided context during interaction. We introduce a framework that disentangles two distinct triggers of political sycophancy: opinion (aligning with explicit narratives) and identity (stereotyping based on demographic labels). Using 450 manually-checked political dilemmas as controlled probes, we evaluate 13 instruction-tuned LLMs. We uncover a dissociation: a model's susceptibility to explicit opinions does not necessarily predict its susceptibility to identity cues, and vice versa. When both signals are present, their effects are generally sub-additive rather than simply additive. Additionally,

translated_title: 身份与观点如何塑造大语言模型中的政治谄媚行为
translated_abstract: 随着大语言模型（LLM）越来越多地鼓励用户披露个人资料以获得定制化帮助，衡量其政治立场对齐变得日益重要。然而，许多现有的用于评估政治行为的基准依赖于封闭式问题，无法充分捕捉模型在交互过程中如何根据用户提供的上下文调整自身立场。我们提出了一个框架，将政治谄媚的两种不同触发因素区分开来：观点（迎合明确的叙述）和身份（基于人口统计标签的刻板印象）。使用450个经过人工核验的政治困境作为受控探针，我们评估了13个指令微调的大语言模型。我们发现了一种解离现象：模型对明确观点的易感性并不一定能预测其对身份线索的易感性，反之亦然。当两种信号同时存在时，它们的影响通常呈次可加性，而非简单的叠加。此外，
tldr: 该研究提出一个区分“观点迎合”与“身份刻板印象”两种政治谄媚触发因素的评估框架，通过对450个人工核验的政治困境和13个指令微调LLM的测试，发现模型对这两类线索的易感性相互解离，且两者同时存在时效应呈次可加性而非简单叠加。
en_tdlr: This study introduces a framework that disentangles opinion-based and identity-based triggers of political sycophancy in LLMs, revealing through 450 manually-checked political dilemmas and 13 instruction-tuned models that susceptibility to these two cues is dissociated, and their combined effects are generally sub-additive rather than additive.
